title: Pullback compatibility of the supported-Hom identification
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $h:X'\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and form the Cartesian square with $Z'=X'\times_XZ$, $i':Z'\hookrightarrow X'$ and $g:Z'\to Z$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let $F$ be a bounded-below complex of etale $A$-module sheaves and let $a\in\mathbf Z$; use the ordinary module derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the inverse and direct images of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and supported cohomology of [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Write
$$
\chi_{i,F}^a:H_Z^a(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)}(i_*A_Z,F[a])
$$
for the canonical supported-Hom identification induced by [lem-amb-closed-support-hom]. Let $c:h^{-1}i_*A_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}i'_*A_{Z'}$ be the canonical closed-immersion exchange, with the canonical identification $g^{-1}A_Z=A_{Z'}$. Then for every $\alpha\in H_Z^a(X,F)$,
$$
\chi_{i',h^{-1}F}^a(h^*\alpha)=h^{-1}(\chi_{i,F}^a(\alpha))\circ c^{-1}.
$$
Here $h^*$ on supported groups is the canonical pullback in the localization sequence [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], and the right side uses exact inverse image and its canonical shift comparison. The same equality holds on the small pro-etale sites for $F_{\mathrm{proet}}=\nu_X^{-1}F$, with $\chi$ the identification of [lem-pur-supported-hom] and the canonical supported-constant comparison there; $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ is [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The two identifications agree under the site comparison: let $\nu^*:H^a_Z(X_{\mathrm{et}},F)\to H^a_Z(X_{\mathrm{proet}},F_{\mathrm{proet}})$ be the map induced by the exact inverse image $\nu_X^{-1}$ on derived supported sections, and $\gamma:\nu_X^{-1}i_*A_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*A_Z$ the canonical supported-constant comparison; then $\chi^{a,\mathrm{proet}}_{i,F_{\mathrm{proet}}}(\nu^*\alpha)=\nu_X^{-1}(\chi^a_{i,F}(\alpha))\circ\gamma^{-1}$, and likewise on $X'$. These comparisons commute with $h^*$ and with $c$, so the etale equality is carried to the pro-etale one. No finiteness hypothesis on $h$ or on $X'$ and no purity isomorphism is assumed.

source.place: Section 9, Theorem 9.4 and its Ext proof on pp. 66–67, with Example 9.5; explicit pullback compatibility formulated by the agent from the kernel-of-restriction construction

proof.text: Use three instances of the same notation: $L=h^{-1}$ on etale modules, $L=h^{-1}$ on pro-etale modules, and $L=\nu_X^{-1}$ from etale to pro-etale modules. Their exactness and their canonical identifications $LA_X=A_{X'}$ (respectively $A_{X,\mathrm{proet}}$) are supplied by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], and [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. They therefore induce derived functors by termwise application and commute with shifts, by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Write $P=i_*A_Z$, $P'=i'_*A_{Z'}$ in the first two cases; in the third case $P$ and $P'$ mean the etale and pro-etale versions on the same scheme. We shall prove the compatibility for these three exact inverse images simultaneously.

source.place: Constant module inverse images; ringed-site inverse image and its termwise derived functor

proof.text: Put $U=X\setminus Z$ and $U'=X'\setminus Z'$. On the etale site, [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] applied to $A_X$, with the canonical identifications $j^{-1}A_X=A_U$ and $i^{-1}A_X=A_Z$ of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](1), gives $j_!A_U\xrightarrow{\epsilon}A_X\xrightarrow{\rho}P\to0$, with $\epsilon$ the open counit and $\rho$ constant restriction. On the pro-etale site precisely this cokernel presentation, with these maps and without any quasi-compactness hypothesis on $j$, is [lem-pur-proetale-supported-constant-presentation]. Use the same presentations for the primed pairs. Only this constant-coefficient presentation is needed; no localization assertion for arbitrary pro-etale sheaves is invoked.

source.place: Tag 095L, lemma-ses-associated-to-open; pro-etale constant presentation separately cited

proof.text: For the first instance of $L$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules] identifies $L(j_!A_U)$ with $j'_!A_{U'}$; for the second use [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]; for the third use [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. These canonical open comparisons identify $L\epsilon$ with $\epsilon'$: transposing the two maps by the open adjunction gives in both cases the identity of the pulled-back coefficient unit. Exactness from step 1 and the cokernel presentations of step 2 now give a unique isomorphism $d:LP\xrightarrow{\sim}P'$ satisfying $d\,L\rho=\rho'$ after the constant-unit identification. This is the canonical closed exchange $c$, or the site comparison $\gamma$, respectively. Indeed the adjoint definition of exchange [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] and its pro-etale version from [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] send the constant $1$ to $1$ after restriction to the closed pair; their composites with $L\rho$ are therefore $\rho'$. Since $L\rho$ is epic, this identifies them with $d$. The site comparison is identified by the identical constant-restriction calculation.

source.place: Tag 03S6, lemma-shriek-base-change, adjunction proof; cokernel uniqueness applied to the coefficient unit

proof.text:
For a module sheaf $M$, precomposition with $\rho$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(P,M)$ with the kernel of $\operatorname{Hom}(A_X,M)\to\operatorname{Hom}(j_!A_U,M)$. The etale open adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] and its pro-etale counterpart [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero] identify the latter Hom with $M(U)$. A module map $A_X\to M$ is determined by the image of the global section $1$; its inverse sends $s\in M(X)$ to the sectionwise map $a\mapsto as|_V$ on each object $V$. Under these identifications precomposition with $\epsilon$ is restriction: $(\varphi\rho\epsilon)_U(1)=0$, and for an arbitrary map $\beta:A_X\to M$ its restriction is $(\beta\epsilon)_U(1)=\beta_X(1)|_U$. Thus
$$\theta_M:\operatorname{Hom}(P,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma_Z(X,M),\qquad\varphi\longmapsto(\varphi\rho)_X(1)$$
is an additive natural isomorphism, where the kernel is exactly the definition in [def-pur-support-cohomology]. The same formula defines $\theta'$ on the target site.

source.place: Theorem 9.4, Ext proof p. 67, and Example 9.5 p. 66; module maps evaluated at 1

proof.text:
Let $\lambda_M:\Gamma_Z(X,M)\to\Gamma_{Z'}(X',LM)$ be the map on kernels induced by inverse image of sections and restriction to the open complement, using the same notation for site comparison. For $\varphi:P\to M$, the identity $d^{-1}\rho'=L\rho$ of step 3 gives
$$\theta'_{LM}(L\varphi\circ d^{-1})=(L\varphi\circ L\rho)(1)=\lambda_M((\varphi\rho)(1))=\lambda_M\theta_M(\varphi).$$
The middle equality is simply the map of sections induced by the inverse-image unit; that unit carries $1$ to $1$. The sections lie in the stated kernels because their restrictions to $U'$ are pullbacks of zero. This establishes compatibility before deriving, for all module sheaves and all three choices of $L$.

source.place: Theorem 9.4 proof p. 67; explicit evaluation of the maps on kernels

proof.text: All sites are taken with the small skeleta in the conventions of the statement. The categories of ordinary module sheaves are Grothendieck by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. They have enough injectives: apply [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] to $M[0]$; its degree-zero monomorphism embeds $M$ into an injective object. The bounded-below right-derived universal property [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] derives $\theta$ and $\theta^{-1}$ to mutually inverse maps: the two composites have the identity factorization on complexes, so uniqueness forces them to be identities. Combining this derived identification with [lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof] identifies $H_Z^a(X,F)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(P,F[a])$. This is the canonical $\chi$ in the statement. More explicitly, on an injective resolution $F\to I$ a supported cocycle $s\in\Gamma_Z(X,I^a)$ is sent to the unique $f:P\to I^a$ with $f\rho(1)=s$, regarded as $P[0]\to I[a]$ and followed by the inverse resolution isomorphism. On the etale site this is the supported-Hom identification [lem-amb-closed-support-hom]: applying Hom to the same open-closed presentation computes the kernel of restriction, hence its shifted cone. On the pro-etale site it is [lem-pur-supported-hom]. This fixes the normalization rather than choosing an arbitrary natural isomorphism.

source.place: Example 9.5 and proof of Theorem 9.4, pp. 66–67; derive the displayed kernel/Hom identity

proof.text:
Choose bounded-below injective resolutions $e:F\to I$ and $e':LF\to J$ using [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution]. Exactness of $L$ makes $Le$ a quasi-isomorphism. The K-injective comparison principle [lem-sp-kinjective-comparison-principle] gives a chain map $t:LI\to J$ with $t\,Le$ homotopic to $e'$, unique up to homotopy. Apply step 5 degreewise and then postcompose with $t$: on supported sections the chain map is $s\mapsto\Gamma_{Z'}(t)(\lambda_I(s))$, while on Hom complexes it is
$$f\longmapsto t\circ Lf\circ d^{-1}.$$
The two agree under $\theta,\theta'$. To identify the first with canonical derived supported pullback, apply the universal property of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] to the termwise map $\lambda$ followed by the target derived unit. It gives a unique $R\Gamma_Z\to R\Gamma_{Z'}\circ DL$ with this factorization. Computing it on $I$ gives exactly the displayed map into $J$. This is the canonical map used in the functorial localization sequence [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], since both derive the same kernel-of-restriction transformation. This argument does not require $L$ to preserve injectives.

source.place: Theorem 9.4 functoriality, with the bounded-below comparison made explicit using the derived universal property

proof.text:
For a cocycle $f:P\to I^a$ representing $\alpha$, step 6 represents $\chi(\alpha)$ by $e[a]^{-1}\circ f$, and step 7 represents the pulled-back supported class by $t[a]\circ Lf\circ d^{-1}$. Consequently its target $\chi'$ is
$$e'[a]^{-1}\circ t[a]\circ Lf\circ d^{-1}=(Le)[a]^{-1}\circ Lf\circ d^{-1}=L(\chi(\alpha))\circ d^{-1}.$$
Here $tLe=e'$ in the homotopy category by step 7, and hence also in the derived category. The canonical shift comparison is the one obtained by applying the additive exact functor termwise. Homotopic choices of $t$ induce homotopic maps of both complexes, and boundaries in $f$ give null-homotopic maps out of $P[0]$, as in [lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof]. Thus the equality is independent of resolutions and holds in every integer degree. Specializing $L$ and $d$ gives the etale formula, the pro-etale formula (in particular for etale-origin $F$), and the formula for $\nu^*$ and $\gamma$.

source.place: Theorem 9.4 and Example 9.5; cancellation of the two resolution isomorphisms

proof.text: Finally use [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] to identify $\nu_{X'}^{-1}h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$ with $h_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}\nu_X^{-1}$, and similarly on the open and closed subschemes. It is compatible with composites and the Cartesian identification by its statement. On the supported constant objects the two resulting maps to $i'_*A_{Z'}$ have the same composite with the twice-pulled-back epimorphism $\rho$: both send the constant $1$ to $1$ and restrict the same constant sections. They are equal by epic cancellation. On supported sections, the two transformations agree because the inverse-image units compose and restriction of a section along the two identified composite morphisms agrees. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] carries this equality to their derived transformations. Thus the $c$, $\gamma$, and supported pullback squares commute, and the etale equality of step 8 is carried to the asserted pro-etale equality. Nothing in these constructions requires finiteness of $h$ or $X'$ or invokes purity.
